reference_opening.argument: This video is scam content because it directs viewers to the Forsage BUSD site and explains how to participate through a 10 BUSD investment split into X3 and X4. It presents earnings tied to downline, upline, cross-line, and slot-purchase structures, including large claimed returns, and invites viewers to make contact. The review or truth-check framing and account-statistics demonstration do not remove these promotional instructions and solicitation cues.

opening.argument: Judge, the presentation repeatedly signals investigation rather than certainty. Its title calls itself a plan review and “The Whole Truth,” while the narrator asks, “Are people really earning here?” That wording presents the earnings question as something to examine, not as an unconditional promise. The speaker also directs viewers to inspect an account and its statistics, saying that “you can check anyone's ID,” which invites verification of the claims rather than reliance on the speaker alone. Even the discussion of possible earnings is introduced as an examination of what the system displays, leaving room for the viewer to assess the evidence independently.

rebuttal.rebuttal: The prosecution treats the website address and plan explanation as solicitation, but those details are equally consistent with investigating the claims. The narrator explicitly introduces the exercise by asking whether people are really earning, and the account display is presented as something viewers can inspect. The opening does not establish that the speaker guarantees returns or suppresses uncertainty; it mainly identifies where the claims can be checked.

citations.quote: So come friends now let's check the truth Are people really earning here?
first open Google Chrome in Google Chrome type busd.forsage.io

true_side_reply.rebuttal: The truth-check wording does not neutralize the substance that follows. The speaker gives a 10 BUSD entry structure, explains money from downline and cross-line positions, and describes repeated income. Asking whether people earn is a rhetorical lead-in; it does not warn viewers that the claims may be unreliable or that participation may cause loss. The account display shows what the site reports, not independent verification of those reports.

opening.argument: This is best understood as an operational demonstration of how the platform can be examined. The narrator walks through opening a browser, entering the site, selecting an ID, and viewing the resulting statistics. He explains that viewers can check IDs themselves, then demonstrates the displayed participant and earnings information. The visual material likewise shows a browser page containing a statistics screen and separate diagrams of the X3 and X4 structures. That is instructional and explanatory content about a digital platform's stated operation, not proof that the creator is personally collecting money or making a deceptive promise.

citations.quote: first open Google Chrome in Google Chrome type busd.forsage.io
you can check anyone's ID without the pass

rebuttal.rebuttal: Calling the walkthrough instructional does not change what it teaches. The narration moves from checking an ID to explaining how a viewer invests 10 BUSD across X3 and X4 and how money comes from network positions. The diagrams are not incidental interface documentation; they illustrate the plan's slots and payouts. A tutorial can still function as promotion when its practical lesson is how to enter and earn through the structure.

citations.quote: when you invest 10 BUSd so you want 5BUSd in x3 and 5BUSd in X4
you and you money comes from downline While X4 is working Non working Your upline will also get money from your cross line

true_side_reply.rebuttal: The demonstration is not neutral data processing. It explains the amounts for successive slots, says the first joiner goes to the participant, and describes income as repeating after a slot is purchased. Showing a site and diagrams may be educational in form, but the practical instructions and earnings narrative give viewers a participation model rather than merely describing technology.

citations.quote: So friends, now you don's see the marketing plan of this

you have to purchase only one slot and at least buy one slot only one time

opening.argument: The supplied material does not establish the concrete features needed to call this deceptive commerce. It shows a website statistics page and plan diagrams, but no credential request, no instruction to surrender personal information, and no demonstrated transfer by a viewer. The narrator describes the displayed system and says its IDs can be checked. The presentation therefore supports an interpretation of discussing an external platform and its advertised structure, while the evidence does not independently establish that any displayed result is genuine, that a viewer will lose money, or that the speaker controls the service.

citations.quote: in this you can check anyone's ID without the pass

rebuttal.rebuttal: The prosecution need not show a password request or a completed transfer to identify the content's central mechanism. The narration itself states that participation begins with a 10 BUSD investment, divides it into X3 and X4, and links income to downline, upline, and cross-line positions. Those are not ordinary retail features merely because the video also displays a statistics page.

citations.quote: when you invest 10 BUSd so you want 5BUSd in x3 and 5BUSd in X4
you and you money comes from downline While X4 is working Non working Your upline will also get money from your cross line

true_side_reply.rebuttal: The missing credential request is beside the point. The relevant evidence is the promised structure: entry money is split between X3 and X4, slots double in amount, and the narration describes repeated income and large totals. The absence of a completed viewer transaction does not make those recruitment-linked payout claims ordinary commerce, and the site display does not independently validate them.
